The player already stood adjacent to all 3 frames without completing, so plain adjacency isn't it. New hypothesis: SPACE while adjacent & facing a frame "collects" its blue core. Player is at (7,6) facing left; left eye is (7,4). One LEFT → (7,5) adjacent & facing it, then SPACE.

def snap(frame):
    out={}
    for n in frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        b=n['boundary']; rs=[p[0] for p in b]; cs=[p[1] for p in b]
        out.setdefault(n['color'],[]).append((min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs),n['pixels']))
    return out
before=snap(current_frame)
res=action(['LEFT'])
print('after LEFT:', {k:current_frame.segmentation and snap(current_frame)[k] for k in ('N','W','b','c','G') if k in snap(current_frame)})
r1=last_action_result
res=action(['SPACE'])
r2=last_action_result
after=snap(current_frame)
print('after SPACE: N',after.get('N'),'W',after.get('W'))
print('b cores:',after.get('b'))
print('c/G frames:',after.get('c'),after.get('G'))
print('r1', {k:r1.get(k) for k in ('no_impact','done','level_completed','game_over')})
print('r2', {k:r2.get(k) for k in ('no_impact','done','level_completed','game_over','board_changed')})
